parameters.content:
### Per-step block
Each step is: set its input and start time, call its sub-workflow, then log ok or log the failure, and on to the next step. A failure logs its error, finishes the run with ok = false and responds. Steps 0 to 9 are built (step 0 runs before step 1); steps 10 to 16 copy this block. Steps 6 to 9 are one sub-workflow with one model call: it logs four rows, the call's `llm` and tokens on step 6 (steps 7 to 9 log ms 0), and a failure logs the row of the lowest `step N:` in its error text (6 when none). The webhook body's optional `temperature` and `seed` (defaults 0 and 42) go to step 1. Its optional `profile_id` (null means the default profile) goes to step 0. Its optional `guide` (`any`, `bjcp`, `ba`; null when not sent) goes to step 2. Step 1 also logs tokens and the `llm` details (model, tries, ms), then saves the brief in `app.brief` and sets `app.run.brief_id`.

### Test data · editor run
Pin this on `POST recipe-pipeline` (open the node, use the output panel's edit / mock-data control, paste the JSON, save), then click *Execute workflow*.
Runs for real and writes `app.run` with `eval_id = 'editor-b01'`; remove with `delete from app.run where eval_id like 'editor-%'`. Set `request` to `""` to see the failure path. Webhook calls ignore the pin.

```json
[{"headers": {"content-type": "application/json"}, "params": {}, "query": {}, "body": {"request": "I want a classic West Coast IPA that is properly bitter. Make it 20 litres at about 6.5 % ABV.", "brief_id": "editor-b01"}}]
```
